subject: Security KMS follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Carter <alice.carter@finbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Dec 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Security KMS follow-up and next steps

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk through FinBank's ingestion and retention flow. Quick recap from our side and next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Ask captured: you want details on encryption (at-rest + in-transit), KMS/HSM support, and whether we offer customer-managed keys (CMK). You also asked for our SOC 2 report and to start the vendor security questionnaire.
- What I'll send now: a short KMS FAQ (attached) that outlines our supported modes (hosted KMS, customer-managed envelope keys, and HSM-backed options) and an outline of how we handle envelope + per-customer keys.
- Immediate next steps:
  1) I've attached our vendor_security_questionnaire.pdf - please confirm receipt and flag any items you want us to prioritise.
  2) I'll pull our SOC 2 Type II attestation link and share the access instructions for your security team.
  3) If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min deep-dive with our security engineer (Aditya) to go into the KMS/HSM architecture and key lifecycle.

Short answers to the KMS questions you raised on the call:
- At-rest: All customer data at rest is encrypted using AES-256. We support envelope encryption where the data encryption key (DEK) is wrapped by a Key Encryption Key (KEK).
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+/mTLS for service-to-service; public API endpoints are TLS 1.3.
- Customer-managed keys: Yes - we support customer-managed keys via common cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). We also support Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) flows and envelope encryption.
- HSM: For customers requiring HSM-backed key control we offer integration with Cloud HSM-backed KMS providers and can support customer HSM via established BYOK processes.

Attachments: vendor_security_questionnaire.pdf (filled copy requested), redwood_kms_faq.pdf (high-level), SOC2_Remote_Access_Instructions.txt (access steps).

Proposed times for the security deep-dive: Tue 12/29 9-9:30am PT or Wed 12/30 10-10:30am PT - let me know what works and I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

Thanks Camila, appreciate the summary. A few clarifying Qs from our security/compliance team before we schedule the deeper call: 

1) Can you confirm whether customer-managed keys (CMK) allow FinBank to rotate keys independently of Redwood control (i.e., we can revoke/rotate without Redwood being a required step)?
2) Do you expose key usage logs (who/when keys were used) that we can ingest into our SIEM?
3) For HSM-backed keys, do you support FIPS 140-2 Level 3 attestations (or equivalent) and can you provide evidence?
4) Where is the root KEK stored for the hosted option - do you use a multi-tenant KMS or a separate key per customer?
5) Please share the SOC 2 Type II report or a way for our team to access it (either link or secure portal).

We will also upload a vendor security questionnaire on our side, sending it tonight. Would prefer to have the deeper technical call with Aditya present so we can dive into key lifecycle and logging.

Best,
Alice Carter
Sr. Information Security Manager | FinBank
alice.carter@finbank.com

Hi Alice,

Great questions - quick answers below and happy to expand on the call with Aditya.

1) CMK rotation/revocation: Yes, when configured for CMK/BYOK the customer has sole control of the KEK in their KMS. FinBank can rotate or revoke keys in your KMS - if you revoke the KEK the wrapped DEKs become unrecoverable (this is expected behaviour for customer-controlled keys). Redwood does not store or retain plaintext KEKs for CMK configurations.

2) Key usage logs: We publish Key Usage and Key Access logs (Cloud KMS access logs) and can provide a delivery pattern to ship them to your SIEM (S3/GCS export or direct SIEM ingestion via our log forwarder). We also expose audit records in the console for admin review.

3) HSM attestations: For cloud HSM integrations we use provider attestations (e.g., AWS CloudHSM FIPS 140-2 Level 3 where available). We can share the vendor attestation PDFs and the configuration matrix.

4) Root KEK storage for hosted option: Hosted customers get a per-customer KEK (not a single multi-tenant root). KEKs are stored in a hardened KMS with role separation; we can share architecture docs on the call.

5) SOC 2: Here is a secure link to request access to our SOC 2 Type II: https://redwood.sharepoint.com/sites/security/SOC2/request-access. I've attached SOC2_Remote_Access_Instructions.txt with the steps your team can follow to request and download the attestation.

Next steps:
- I'll schedule a 30-minute technical deep-dive tomorrow at 9am PT with Aditya - sending invite now (accept if that works).
- We'll import your vendor questionnaire into our tracker and aim to return responses within 3 business days after we receive the uploaded copy.

If there are any specific fields in the questionnaire you want prioritized (e.g., KMS logs, attestation copies, encryption configuration), highlight them in the upload and Marissa will own the tracking.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
